title: Close-area corridor MPC: linear MPC with OSQP in an ESDF half-plane corridor on the arena A*, vs the carrot follower
summary: Replaces the close-area-arena A* carrot follower with a linear MPC path follower and measures the difference. Model: state p, v; input the velocity setpoint, with the exact zero-order-hold discretisation of the arena's first-order velocity lag (tau 0.15 s), so the output is sent to send_setpoint() unchanged. Horizon 20 x 0.1 s, per-axis boxes on velocity (1.4 m/s) and on acceleration via |u - v| <= tau a_max, tracking cost on a reference marched along the A* path with the carrot's ESDF speed rule. Corridor per horizon step from the same 0.1 m grid as the ESDF: nearest-point separating half-planes (safe-flight-corridor style, no ellipsoid) offset by radius + 0.05 m, plus a box that keeps it inside the 2 m search radius; rows soft with a heavy slack penalty. OSQP with fixed sparsity, per-step update of q, l, u and corridor values, warm start from the shifted previous solution. bench.py compares carrot vs MPC (and cold-start, no-corridor and constant-speed ablations) on 50 random and 50 narrow_gap layouts, scored on truth, and plots a narrow_gap run with both paths and the corridor. Synthetic arena, known map, truth pose.
verified: ran 2026-11-09 with CPython 3.11.15 + numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 / osqp 1.1.3 on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 26.6.2), in the sample venv: bench.py --layouts 50 --seed 0 wrote results/mpc_compare_0.json/.md and results/mpc_narrow_gap_0_run32.png (wall 381.9 s; the PNG was re-drawn once with a corrected panel title through bench.plot, same run and outcomes). A second astar_mpc pass over the 50 narrow_gap layouts gave identical per-run outcome, min clearance, path length and time to goal (checked in the console, not saved). Every number in README is from results/. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the venv (model vs the 50 Hz arena vehicle within 2 cm; narrow_gap run 0 matches results), 1 skipped under plain python3 without numpy. osqp license read from the installed wheel metadata (Apache-2.0). No arena file was edited. Layouts, vehicle and sensor are simulated, the map is known and the pose is truth; no SITL, no flight computer timing, no estimator faults.
shows: Linear MPC (OSQP) tracking the A* path inside a soft half-plane corridor from the grid, vs the A* carrot follower: outcomes, clearance, tracking error, solve time with and without warm start
runtime: ~6.5 min for 50 layouts x 2 families x 6 followers
key_result: [50 layouts per family, seed 0](README.md#results-ran-2026-11-09-apple-m3-max-cpython-31115-numpy-246-scipy-1171-osqp-113): carrot and MPC both 100 % reached, 0 % collision on random and narrow_gap, tracking p95 0.053 vs 0.054 m; MPC median time to goal 21.97 vs 24.23 s on narrow_gap; QP 0.22 ms median / 0.46 ms p95 warm, 0.73 / 1.04 ms cold on an M3 Max
